name: primitive_set_erdos
claim_latex: For any $x$, if $A \subset [x, \infty)$ is a primitive set of integers (no distinct element divides another) then $\sum_{a \in A} \frac{1}{a \log a} < 1 + o(1)$, where the $o(1)$ term tends to $0$ as $x \to \infty$.

literature_resolution.citation: B. Alexeev, K. Barreto, Y. Li, J. D. Lichtman, L. Price, J. I. Shah, Q. Tang, T. Tao, 'Primitive sets and von Mangoldt chains: Erdős Problem #1196 and beyond', arXiv:2605.00301 (May 2026)
literature_resolution.statement: Theorem 1.1: if $A$ is primitive and $A \subset [x, \infty)$ then $\sum_{a \in A} \frac{1}{a \log a} \leq 1 + O(1/\log x)$. Combined with the k-almost-prime lower-bound engine (f(N_k) -> 1 from below), the limit of the sup is exactly 1.
literature_resolution.method: Markov chains over divisibility chains with von Mangoldt weights (log n = sum of Lambda(d) over d | n); core sub-invariance inequality reported as Lemma 3.3(iii). Method suggested by output of GPT-5.4 Pro; human-verified. This was Erdős problem #1196 (Erdős–Sárközy–Szemerédi, 1966).
literature_resolution.confidence: arXiv preprint as of July 2026, authors include Lichtman and Tao; not yet journal-published

benchmark_mode: This claim is now a THEOREM. The spec is retained as a REDISCOVERY BENCHMARK: a proof loop that can independently reconstruct (or verify step-by-step) the von Mangoldt chain argument calibrates harness changes. A verified counterexample witness is mathematically impossible — witness_valid == 1 on this problem indicates a bug in library.primitive_set_witness and must be treated as such, never as a result.

given_facts.sign_disambiguation: UPPER bound on the sum, STRICTLY LESS THAN. The constant $e^\gamma \pi/4 \approx 1.399$ is positive; this fact does NOT contradict the conjecture (which posits a tighter bound of 1).
given_facts.citation: J. D. Lichtman, 'A proof of the Erdős primitive set conjecture', Forum of Mathematics Pi 11 (2023) e31, arXiv:2202.02384, Theorem 1.5. Historical chain: Erdős 1935 proved boundedness; Erdős–Zhang 1993 (Proc. AMS 117) proved f(A) < 1.84 unconditionally; Lichtman–Pomerance 2019 (arXiv:1806.02250) proved f(A) < e^{\gamma} \approx 1.781 unconditionally.
warns: This is an upper bound, not a lower bound. It is consistent with the conjecture. Misreading it as a lower bound is a sign error.
The 1.399 constant is Lichtman 2023, NOT Erdős–Zhang 1993 (their constant was 1.84, with no min-element restriction). A previous version of this ledger misattributed it.

given_facts.statement: If $A_k = \{n \in \mathbb{N} : \Omega(n) = k\}$ (integers with exactly $k$ prime factors counted with multiplicity), then $\sum_{a \in A_k} \frac{1}{a \log a} \geq 1 + O(k^{-1/2 + o(1)})$.
given_facts.sign_disambiguation: The big-O term $O(k^{-1/2 + o(1)})$ is UNSIGNED — it could be positive or negative. The inequality reads: the sum is at least $1$ minus some quantity bounded in absolute value by $k^{-1/2+o(1)}$, NOT $1$ plus a positive quantity. Concluding $\text{sum} > 1$ from this fact is a SIGN ERROR.
given_facts.citation: stated as fact F2 in the user prompt
warns: This is the failure mode of the ChatGPT writeup committed at tests/fixtures/chatgpt_primitive_set_round0.md. Any chain that concludes 'sum > 1' from this fact alone, without an additional positivity argument for the big-O term, MUST be flagged BLOCKING.

given_facts.statement: For $A_k = \{n \in \mathbb{N} : \Omega(n) = k\}$, $\sum_{a \in A_k} \frac{1}{a \log a} = 1 - (c + o(1)) \frac{k^2}{2^k}$ where $c = \frac{\log 2}{4} d \approx 0.0656$ for an explicit constant $d \approx 0.37869$.
given_facts.sign_disambiguation: The leading correction is $-(c+o(1)) k^2 / 2^k$ with $c > 0$, so the sum is STRICTLY LESS THAN 1 for every large $k$, approaching $1$ from BELOW as $k \to \infty$. This is the canonical 'extremal-looking' primitive set; even it does not violate the conjecture.
given_facts.citation: O. Gorodetsky, J. D. Lichtman, M. D. Wong, 'On Erdős sums of almost primes', C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris (2024), arXiv:2303.08277. Same paper DISPROVES the Banks–Martin monotonicity conjecture: f(N_k) attains a global minimum (at k = 6) and is eventually monotonically INCREASING toward 1.
warns: F3 directly contradicts any claim that A_k is a counterexample. F3 is consistent with F2 once F2's unsigned-O is read correctly.

given_facts.statement: For every primitive set $A$, $\sum_{a \in A} \frac{1}{a \log a} \leq \sum_{p \text{ prime}} \frac{1}{p \log p} = 1.6366\ldots$ — the primes maximize the Erdős sum (the original 1935/1988 conjecture, Erdős problem #164).
given_facts.sign_disambiguation: NON-STRICT upper bound, attained exactly by $A = \mathcal{P}$. Unconditional — no min-element restriction.
given_facts.citation: J. D. Lichtman, Forum of Mathematics Pi 11 (2023) e31, arXiv:2202.02384. Short new proof also in arXiv:2605.00301.
warns: Global ceiling: any tail bound proved must be consistent with 1.6366. A 'counterexample' to the basic form would contradict a published theorem — treat as a bug.

given_facts.statement: Write $A_q = \{a \in A : p(a) = q\}$ where $p(a)$ is the SMALLEST prime factor of $a$. If $q \notin A$ then $f(A_q) < e^{\gamma} g(q)$ where $g(q) = \frac{1}{q}\prod_{p<q}(1 - \frac{1}{p})$ is the natural density of $\{n : p(n) = q\}$. The strata are disjoint so $\sum_q g(q) \leq 1$, giving $f(A) < e^{\gamma}$.
given_facts.sign_disambiguation: Per-stratum UPPER bound, strict, requires $q \notin A$ (if $q \in A$ then $A_q = \{q\}$ by primitivity and $f(A_q) = f(q)$ exactly).
given_facts.citation: J. D. Lichtman, C. Pomerance, 'The Erdős conjecture for primitive sets', Proc. AMS Ser. B 6 (2019) 1–14, arXiv:1806.02250, Proposition 2.1.
warns: This is THE reusable lemma shape: per-least-prime-factor stratum bound proportional to a density, then densities sum to at most 1. The e^{\gamma} factor is what the von Mangoldt chain method replaces with 1 + o(1).

given_facts.statement: THEOREM (resolves this spec's claim): if $A$ is primitive and $A \subset [x, \infty)$, $x \geq 2$, then $\sum_{a \in A} \frac{1}{a \log a} \leq 1 + O(1/\log x)$.
given_facts.sign_disambiguation: One-sided UPPER bound with positive error term $O(1/\log x)$. Together with F3's lower-bound engine ($f(N_k \cap (x,\infty)) \to 1$), the limit of the sup is exactly 1.
given_facts.citation: Alexeev, Barreto, Li, Lichtman, Price, Shah, Tang, Tao, arXiv:2605.00301 (May 2026), Theorem 1.1.
warns: This fact resolves the claim. Any 'counterexample' witness on this problem contradicts a theorem — witness_valid == 1 means a verifier bug.
A rediscovery-benchmark proof must not simply cite this fact for the central step; the point of the benchmark is to reconstruct the argument.

given_facts.statement: Core sub-invariance inequality of the von Mangoldt chain method: for integers $m \geq 1$, $\sum_{q} \frac{\Lambda(q)}{q \log(mq) \log(2mq)} \leq \frac{1}{\log(2m)}$, summed over prime powers $q$, where $\Lambda$ is the von Mangoldt function. Using $\log n = \sum_{d \mid n} \Lambda(d)$, this lets a Markov chain over divisibility chains dominate $f(A)$ by the chain's initial mass.
given_facts.sign_disambiguation: UPPER bound, unconditional, uniform in $m$. MEDIUM CONFIDENCE on the exact displayed form (extracted from an automated HTML fetch of arXiv:2605.00301, reported as Lemma 3.3(iii)); the structural role (sub-invariance / supermartingale property of von Mangoldt weights along divisor chains) is high confidence. Re-derive before formal use.
warns: The exact log(mq) vs log(2mq) placement should be re-derived or checked against the PDF before being used as a cited step in a proof.
